problem_type: Media timeline action ownership and executable capability
symptom: User requested removal of the hover notch; pre-implementation regression also proves queued/running old results and non-media URLs advertise a timeline action. Real Electron native-drag acceptance observed no dragstart/drop: XYFlow moved the whole node and attempted overlapping frame 12 on baseline [0,60].
direct_cause: BaseGenerationNode owns a separate hover handle; the affordance predicate only checks URL/error while clip construction separately rejects active generation. FloatingToolbarFrame only stops React pointerdown; XYFlow owns native mousedown and requires its existing nodrag/no-pan classes.
class_root: Timeline action installation and executable-media eligibility lack a common boundary shared by media toolbars. Shared toolbar controls did not explicitly own native gestures independently of their parent canvas node.
affected_population: Generated/imported/derived images and videos, audio results and primary-version switches
internal_only_reason: Internal UI ownership and application clip-state invariant; no external API or dependency changes.
invariants: Each eligible selected media node has one timeline toolbar icon and no hover notch.
Click and drag consume a live eligible primary result.
All media toolbar variants install the same action; unsupported and active-generation results cannot advertise it.
Image result toolbar routing depends on media type rather than a node-kind whitelist, preserving legacy image results.
Every shared node toolbar excludes XYFlow node-drag and canvas-pan; the timeline icon emits native MIME dragstart/drop without moving its source node.

door_reduction.why_not: Initial gesture scan counted 5 doors; expanded ownership scan also includes the image-toolbar host, executable clip construction predicate and existing timeline builders (9 total). Preview cards and global track drops are distinct existing surfaces; they retain the shared adoption/clip construction boundaries. Node image presentation and click/drag need distinct calls, all installed in the one toolbar shell. Native gesture ownership census adds 7 toolbar consumers (16 combined doors). All share the same FloatingToolbarFrame filter; distinct toolbar content remains separate.

generality_proof: FloatingToolbarShell is shared by image/video/audio result toolbars. A single node-owned action reads live state and gates both gestures through the common predicate, which reuses clip construction.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Install one timeline action for every node-owned toolbar.
Authorize executable supported media before presentation and interaction.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Image result routing uses the shared host, including legacy shot/output media shapes; the host installs FloatingToolbarShell with node.id.
All video result routing uses FloatingToolbarShell with node.id.
Audio result toolbar uses the same shell.
Separate preview source cards retain their existing media filtering and adoption-bridge operation.

recurrence.reason: Any media kind or result-state change can repeat the URL-only capability mismatch.
same_class_scan: rg TimelineNotchDragHandle: one component and one mount
Independent toolbar_census traced imports, derivations, versions, panorama, director, clip and artifact surfaces

prevention.invariant: One node-owned media toolbar action; every gesture rechecks the live executable-media predicate. The common toolbar shell uses the existing XYFlow nodrag/no-pan filters for every control.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing or ineligible live result produces no action and cancels stale drag/click.
prevention.strategy: Delete the standalone hover path; automatically compose the action into existing common toolbar ownership and reuse clip construction for eligibility. Reuse existing framework filters at the common shell; native acceptance proves the actual drag channel and unchanged source position.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove hover-only notch component and its BaseGenerationNode event/mount path in the same change.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Reuse existing React native button/drag events and application toolbar/adoption components; no dependency upgrade governs this application invariant.

migration: No persisted state changes. Existing node/result identities and timeline drag payload format are retained.
residual_risks: Real macOS Electron zh/en acceptance passed (40 cases); Windows and packaged application unverified.
